outcome: Cardiometabolic risk factors (blood pressure, insulin, leptin, adiponectin, and lipid concentrations)
cohort: 695 offspring of pregnant women enrolled in the Danish Fetal Origins Cohort in 1988-1989
finding: Birth by Cesarean section was associated with increased odds of overweight or obesity at 20 years and higher serum concentrations of total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, leptin, and Apolipoprotein B, independently of shared risk factors.
mod_finding: Birth by Cesarean section was associated with increased odds of offspring overweight or obesity at 20 years and higher serum concentrations of total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, leptin, and Apolipoprotein B.
